description.en: Yitro was the father of Moses's wife [Tzipporah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/tzipporah1?tab=sources) and a Midianite priest. He served as Moses's advisor in the desert.
description.he: יתרו הוא אבי צפורה, אשת משה, וכוהן מדיין. הוא שימש יועץ למשה בתקופת הנדודים במדבר.

description.he: השמיים נזכרים בפסוקים הראשונים של ספר בראשית, ובמקורות הם לרוב מייצגים את כל מה שנמצא מעל כדור הארץ. כמו כן השמיים נתפסים כמקום שהאל והמלאכים שוכנים בו.
description.en: The Heavens (Shamayim) appear in the first lines of Genesis and are mentioned frequently in the Jewish sources as representing everything above Earth. The Heavens are also understood as the place where God and the angels reside.

The prophet Samuel (Shmuel in Hebrew) led the Israelites before the King Saul, the first king, was anointed. Under his leadership, Israel rose up against the Phillistines. He anointed Saul as king and advised him before secretly anointing David when God decided Saul was no longer fit to be king.
description.he: הנביא שמואל הנהיג את בני ישראל לפני תקופת המלוכה. תחת הנהגתו נלחם עם ישראל בפלישתים. הוא משח את שאול למלך הראשון של ישראל ושימש לו יועץ ונביא, עד שבסתר, במצוות האל, משח את דוד למלך במקומו.

description.en: In Tzav (“Command”), God tells Moses about the sacrifices offered in the Mishkan (Tabernacle), including a meal offering brought by the high priest, guilt offerings, and offerings of thanks. Moses initiates Aaron and Aaron’s sons for priestly service in the Mishkan.
description.he: בפרשת צו מתוארים קורבן עולה, שכל חלקיו (מלבד העור) נשרפים כליל על המזבח; קורבן מנחה, שהוא קורבן מן הצומח; וכן קורבנות חטאת, אשם, שלמים ותודה. נאסר על בני ישראל לאכול דם וחלב – חלקים מן הבהמה המוקרבים תמיד על המזבח. משה מקדיש את אהרן ובניו לכהונה בסדרת קורבנות המובאים בשבעת ימי המילואים.

description.en: Bechukotai (“In My Laws”) is the final Torah portion in the Book of Leviticus. It begins describing blessings that follow obedience to God's laws and curses that come with desecration of them. It ends with laws of vows and consecration of people and property.
description.he: בפרשת בְּחֻקֹּתַי, הפרשה האחרונה בספר ויקרא, מתואר השכר המובטח לבני ישראל אם ישמרו את דיני התורה: שגשוג כלכלי וחקלאי, שלום והצלחה צבאית והשראת שכינה. הפרשה מאריכה בתיאור העונשים והקללות שיבואו על בני ישראל אם לא ישמרו את דיני התורה: שפל כלכלי, רעב, מחלות, תבוסה במלחמות וגלות. אלוהים מבטיח שיזכור את בריתו עם האבות והארץ, והפרשה מסתיימת בדיני ערכין באדם ובקרקעות.

description.en: Miketz (“After”) follows Joseph as he interprets Pharaoh's dreams and rises to become second-in-command to Pharaoh. When Joseph’s brothers come to Egypt seeking food during a famine, Joseph accuses them of spying. He insists that they return with their youngest brother, Benjamin, and later plants a goblet in Benjamin’s bag.
description.he: בפרשת מקץ יוסף פותר את חלומותיו של פרעה ועולה לגדולה בתפקיד המשנה למלך. אחי יוסף מגיעים למצרים לקנות אוכל בשל הרעב הכבד השורר בארץ כנען, ויוסף מאשים אותם בריגול. הוא דורש שישובו למצרים עם אחיהם הצעיר בנימין. יוסף נותן להם אוכל ושולח אותם בשלום, אך מסתיר גביע כסף באמתחת בנימין ומאשים אותו בגנבה.

description.en: Tikkun means “repair” or “mend” and is used alongside the word olam (world) to express the Jewish responsibility to “repair the world.” Tikkun also refers to specific texts read on various holidays, including the seventh day of Passover and on Shavuot.
description.he: הביטוי תיקון עולם מסמל את האחריות היהודית לשכלול המוסריות האנושית. המונח "תיקון" לבדו קשור בטקסטים מסוימים הנקראים בכמה מועדים, דוגמת שביעי של פסח ושבועות.

description.en: Welcoming guests (hachnasat orchim) is an important act of loving-kindness (gemilut chasadim). Welcoming guests also involves housing and feeding guests—with a friendly and welcoming disposition.
description.he: הכנסת אורחים היא רכיב חשוב בתוך המצווה הכללית של גמילות חסדים. מלבד פתיחת הבית לאורח, הכנסת אורחים כוללת לינה ומזון, כל זאת מתוך אהבה ובסבר פנים יפות.

description.en: The High Priest was the head priest of the Israelites, beginning with the biblical [Aaron](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/aaron?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) and continuing through the Second Temple period. The High Priest had a special role in the [Mishkan](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) and Temple service, and wore unique garments detailed in the [book of Exodus](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.28.3?ven=The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).

description.en: Pinchas was a priest best known for his violent reaction to Israelite worship of the god Ba'al Pe'or. As this worship was associated with sexual relationships between Israelite men and Moabite and Midianite women, he killed one such couple mid-intercourse. Pinchas was a leader of the Israelites when they went into the Promised Land.
description.he: פינחס נודע בעיקר בשל תגובתו האלימה נגד המשתחווים לבעל פעור. פולחן בעל פעור היה כרוך במגע מיני בין גברים מבני ישראל ונשים מואביות ומדייניות, ופינחס הרג זוג כזה בשעת מעשה. הוא היה מבכירי ההנהגה של עם ישראל בכניסתם לארץ המובטחת.

description.en: Vayigash (“He Approached”) opens as Judah pleads with Joseph not to keep Benjamin as a prisoner. Joseph reveals his true identity to his brothers, crying and kissing them. The brothers bring Jacob from Canaan to Egypt, and Jacob and his children settle in Goshen. The portion ends as Joseph buys most of Egypt’s land in exchange for food.
description.he: בפרשת ויגש יהודה מתחנן לפני יוסף שישחרר את בנימין ממאסר. יוסף מגלה לאחיו את זהותו, והם בוכים ומתפייסים. אחי יוסף מביאים את יעקב אביהם מכנען למצרים, ויעקב ובניו מתיישבים בגושן. יוסף קונה את רוב אדמות מצרים תמורת מזון שאגר בשנות השובע.

description.en: The returning light is formed when the [partition](/topics/partition2) of a particular [level](/topics/level) of existence rebuffs the supernal light, returning it to its source in the manner of a light refracting off a mirror. This returning light is generated through the resistance of the receiving entity to receiving the supernal light. The returning light does not disappear but rather [enclothes](/topics/enclothe) the supernal light, which is then manifest as a new vessel for the supernal light. All the [levels](/topics/level) and [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf) of creation are formed through [enclothing](/topics/enclothe) supernal, or “direct light” in the receiving entity’s returning light.

Freedom is a concept prevalent throughout Jewish texts. The term is often associated with the biblical story of the Exodus, in which the Israelites were freed from slavery in Egypt, as well as with the ability to perform good deeds and make positive choices.
description.he: חירות היא מושג מורכב ורב-גוני ביהדות אשר משמעותו התפתחה במרוצת השנים. חשיבותה של החירות ביהדות מודגשת היטב ברעיון התשובה ובסיפור יציאת מצרים, בו מתואר כיצד עם ישראל כולו יצא מעבדות והפך לעם חופשי. בנוסף, מושג החירות קשור למושג הבחירה החופשית של האדם והיחס בין ידיעת האל מראש את העתיד לבין חירותו של האדם לפעול על פי מצפונו.

description.en: The [seven lower ones](/topics/seven-lower-ones) of [*Abba* and *Imma*](/topics/abba-and-imma), that is, their ear nose and mouth, are called *Yisrael* *Sabba* and *Tevuna*. Initially, at the time of the [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision) of the [gaze](/topics/gaze1) of the [eyes](/topics/eyes4) of [*Abba* and *Imma*](/topics/abba-and-imma) towards one another, *Yisrael* *Sabba* and *Tevuna* and [*Abba* and *Imma*](/topics/abba-and-imma) are united in a single [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1). Subsequently, however, when [*Abba* and *Imma*](/topics/abba-and-imma) return to a back-to-back [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision), *Yisrael* *Sabba* and *Tevuna* separate from them and emerge as a special [head](/topics/head2) at the level of the ear nose and mouth, becoming a distinct [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 7, Q & A 50).
Middot literally means “measures,” but it’s typically translated as “character traits,” because a person is defined—or measured—by their character traits.
description.he: מלבד המובן המילולי הפשוט של מידות רוחב או אורך, למילה מידות יש משמעות של תכונות אופי, מפני שהאדם מוגדר – או נמדד – לפי תכונות האופי שלו.

description.en: Cain was the oldest child of Adam and Eve, the first human being born, and a farmer. After his own fruit and vegetable offerings to God were rejected, he killed his brother, the shepherd Abel, whose animal offerings had been accepted. He was then cursed to wander the earth, protected by God from being killed in revenge.
description.he: קין הוא בנם הבכור של אדם וחוה, הראשון בין בני מינו שהוא יילוד אישה, והיה עובד אדמה. הוא ואחיו הצעיר הבל הביאו קורבנות לאל, אך לאחר שנדחה קורבן המנחה שהביא קין מן הצומח, ואילו קורבן הבהמה של הבל נתקבל, רצח קין את הבל אחיו. הוא קולל להיות נע ונד בארץ, אך אלוהים הגן עליו מפני נקמת דם.

Among these are sacrifices entirely burnt on the altar, meal offerings made of flour and oil, peace offerings, and sacrifices brought for sinning inadvertently.
description.he: בפרשת ויקרא אלוהים קורא למשה ומצווה אותו על עבודת הקורבנות. הפרשה פותחת בתיאור קורבנות העולה, המנחה (שאיננה קורבן מן הבהמה אלא מן הצומח) והשלמים, בפירוט כמה אפשרויות להקרבת כל סוג קורבן. לאחר מכן מתוארים קורבנות חטאת ואשם ומפורטים המצבים שבהם מובא כל אחד מן הקורבנות.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Ḥesed* is the fourth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Ḥesed* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) [level](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)). The term *sefirat* *Ḥesed* is also a reference to different [levels](/topics/level) and *sefirot* in lower structures of reality that are all derivatives of the root *sefira* of *Ḥesed* found in the [*direct light*](/topics/direct-light1). This [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) is called *Ḥesed* because it contains the light of giving (*ḥassadim*) that emanates from the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), which precedes *Ḥesed*, the light that is the essence of giving and bestowal on the part of a created being and that did not undergo any constriction. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Ḥesed* is always presented as the right hand of the *partzuf*, the hand that represents bestowal and closeness.

description.en: Sefirat HaOmer (literally, "the counting of the Omer") is the period of 49 days between Passover and Shavuot. Each day is verbally counted off. Traditionally, this period of time is a solemn one, and many avoid celebrations during this calendar period.

description.en:
It is known that as a result of the expansion of the [points](/topics/points) of [*Sag*](/topics/sag) to [*Mah*](/topics/mah1) and [*Ban*](/topics/ban) of the inner [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2), [traces](/topics/traces) of two levels are joined in the [partition](/topics/partition2). These are the first *heh* in [*Sag*](/topics/sag), and the bottom *heh* in the inner [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2). Thus, the [partition](/topics/partition2) is incorporated from two females, [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). For this reason the [partition](/topics/partition2) was given the name feminine waters, since from this point onwards it incorporates these two females in every [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision) it performs with the supernal light (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 6, Q & A 15). 
The meaning of feminine waters is that it causes a [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision). It is always an expression of [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), and [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), or *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba). For the female is instituted in the [light](/topics/light2) of the [back side](/topics/back-side) of *Imma*, which is attached only to the [light of giving](/topics/light-of-giving) and which rebuffs [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). Accordingly, she does not turn her face towards the male to receive the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), unless she is forced by some factor to do so. This factor is an expression of *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba), to which the [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) has a connection, to illuminate it with the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), due to the relationship between [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) and the *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba) of the [direct light](/topics/direct-light1). Consequently, when the *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba) ascends to her for feminine waters, her [back side](/topics/back-side) immediately stops, and she turns her face to the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), to receive from it the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). She thus engages in a face-to-face [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision) with it (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 7, Q & A 35).

description.en: Terumah (“Donation”) opens as God tells Moses to collect donated materials in order to build a dwelling place for God called the Mishkan (Tabernacle). God describes how to build the vessels that will fill the Mishkan - including the ark, table, menorah, and sacrificial altar - as well as the Mishkan’s walls and curtains.
description.he: פרשת תרומה פותחת בפנייה לבני ישראל לתרום חומרים לבניית משכן להשראת השכינה בתוך בני ישראל. מבנה המשכן וכליו מתוארים בפירוט רב. המשכן עשוי עצי שיטים המכוסים באריגים ובעורות ממגוון מקורות. מתוארים ארבעה כלים שניצבים בתוך המשכן: ארון, כפורת, שולחן ומנורה. מבנה המשכן מוקף בחצר, ובחצר עומד הכלי המרכזי להקרבת קורבנות – מזבח הנחושת.

description.en: The mikveh is a pool (literally, a “gathering”) of water from a natural source. While the Temples stood, to gain entry into the Temple, to partake of certain sacrifices, or for a couple to be intimate — among other reasons — Jews tried to maintain a status of ritual purity. While there are different kinds of ritual impurity and as many processes to regain a status of ritual purity, immersion in a mikveh, a ritual bath, is an important element in the purification process. Today, the practice of immersion in a mikveh is used to mark life transitions, conversion to Judaism, to ready oneself for Yom Kippur, before birth, and as a central element in the observance of the laws of niddah (the practices surrounding menstruation, intimacy, and ritual purity).
description.he: המקווה הוא בריכה ריטואלית המכילה מים ממקור טבעי (דוגמת מי גשמים). הטבילה במקווה נעשית לשם טהרת אנשים הנחשבים טמאים לפי ההלכה, וכן היא משמשת בתהליך הגיור.

The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Netzaḥ* is the seventh of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – *Keter*, *Ḥokhma*, *Bina*, *Tiferet*, and *Malkhut* – *Netzaḥ* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level) for the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)).  *Netzaḥ* is the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) that completes a structure called the right-hand column in every [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) or world. It is the fourth (thus, the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level)) [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) [level](/topics/level) within the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)). Its essence is therefore that of the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level) which is revealed in the lower part of every *sefira*. As a result, it is considered a “male” [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2), that is, a giving and bestowing [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2), like *Tiferet*. The name *Netzaḥ* comes from the word for victory, *nitzaḥon*. *Netzaḥ* conquers impurity, meaning that, although it is in contact with lower aspects of existence, it simultaneously has the quality of bestowal and giving. This illustrates that *Netzaḥ* is not only undamaged by its involvement in lower realities, but it actually thrives and dominates. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Netzaḥ* is generally presented as the right leg of the [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1).

The world of *Yetzira* is the third of the four worlds (after the supernal world of *Adam Kadmon*) that emanate and descend from one another in the process of creation. Some maintain that its name derives from the Hebrew words for form, *tzura*, or image, *tziyur*, since it is a kind of image or pattern for the final and fourth world, [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2). Each of the worlds corresponds to one of the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). The world of *Yetzira* corresponds to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) or the third [level](/topics/level) of creation. The created beings that dwell in this [level](/topics/level) are the angels called *ḥayot*.

Matot (“Tribes”) opens with laws about vows, and continues to describe the Israelites’ war against the Midianites and the allocation of spoils. The tribes of Reuben and Gad request to dwell outside of the Land of Israel, and Moses acquiesces on the condition that they help conquer it.
description.he: פרשת מטות פותחת בדיני נדרים ושבועות. משה מצווה את בני ישראל להילחם במדיין, ולאחר הניצחון העם מחלק את השלל. בני גד ובני ראובן מבקשים לנחול מחוץ לארץ כנען, בעבר הירדן המזרחי, משום שיש להם מקנה רב. משה מתנגד בתחילה, אך לבסוף מגיע להסדר שלפיו ינחלו השבטים בעבר הירדן המזרחי בתנאי שיעברו חלוצים במלחמה על כיבוש הארץ.

Devarim (“Words”) is the first Torah portion in the Book of Deuteronomy, the final book of the Torah. In it, Moses recounts events from the Israelites’ travels in the desert, like the appointment of judges, the sin of the spies, and the wars with the Emorite kings Sihon and Og.
description.he: דברים היא הפרשה הראשונה בספר דברים, החומש החמישי והאחרון בתורה. בספר מובאים נאומי משה, שבהם הוא מזכיר אירועים מהעבר, סוקר מצוות שכבר ניתנו ומצווה מצוות חדשות. בפרשה משה מספר על הצורך במינוי שופטים להנהגת העם. הוא גם מזכיר את חטא המרגלים, שבו התלונן העם על הכניסה העתידית לארץ כנען, את העונש שהוטל על העם לנדוד במדבר ארבעים שנה ואת מלחמות ישראל במדבר.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is the eighth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Hod* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) [level](/topics/level) for the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1).  *Hod* is the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) which completes the left line or column in every [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) or world. Its essence is that of the fourth [level](/topics/level) ([*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1)). Because of this, and its role of completion, the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is considered female, and possessing the attribute of judgment. The name *Hod* derives from the word *hoda’ah*, thanksgiving, because the feminine (the left side) is grateful for the light that the masculine (the right side) shines on it. This light is the light of giving, which carries the light of wisdom with it, light, which was restricted as a result of the first [constriction](/topics/constriction). In the structure of the [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which correlates with the human body, the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is associated with the left thigh or leg.
Sotah is a halakhic term for a woman suspected of adultery.

Located in ancient Mesopotamia, Babel was the capital city of the Babylonian empire and is notable as the location of the Tower of Babel. Although the Babylonian empire destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem, the subsequent exile ultimately resulted in the creation of the Babylonian Talmud.

description.en: [Hallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Festivals%2C_Rosh_Chodesh%2C_Hallel%2C_Berakhah_before_the_Hallel?lang=en) consists of Psalms 113–118 and is recited on most holidays. There are, however, some holidays on which only part or none of it is recited. These chapters are psalms of thanksgiving and focus on God's communal and personal salvation for those who put their trust in God.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Gevura* is the fifth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Gevura* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) [level](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1))  The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Gevura* is called by this name since it characterizes restraint and constriction. It represents the left column in a process called the rectification of lines, and it is this left column on which the [constriction](/topics/constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)) acts. This placement characterizes the power of restraint that is used to repel the supernal light. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Gevura* is generally presented as the left hand of the *partzuf*.

The [priestly blessing](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Weekday%2C_Shacharit%2C_Amidah%2C_Birkat_Kohanim.1?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) — birkat kohanim in Hebrew —  is a blessing recited by kohanim (those of priestly decent) unto the congregation. Its origins are in [Numbers 6:24–27](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.6.24?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), and these verses are the blessing itself. In Israel, the blessing is recited as part of daily service. Outside of Israel, customs vary as to when it is recited.

There he rose in the court but prophecied the destruction of Babylonia by Persia. He later had visions regarding the coming Macedonian and Seleucid Greek empires.

Achrei Mot (“After The Death”) opens by describing the ritual service of Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement. It then details the prohibitions of offering sacrifices outside of the Mishkan (Tabernacle) and of eating animal blood, and ends with a list of forbidden sexual relations.
description.he: פרשת אחרי מות פותחת בפירוט סדר עבודת יום הכיפורים במשכן: נוסף על קורבנות מיוחדים ועל עבודת הקטורת, עבודת הכהן הגדול כוללת הטלת גורלות לשני שעירי החטאת: אחד מהם מוקרב על גבי המזבח, והאחר - השעיר לעזאזל - נושא את עוונות בני ישראל ונשלח למדבר. הפרשה ממשיכה באיסור לשחוט מחוץ למשכן, באיסור להקריב קורבנות מחוץ למשכן, באיסור אכילת דם, בחובת כיסוי הדם בעוף ובחיה ובטומאת נבלה וטרפה. הפרשה מסתיימת ברשימת איסורי עריות.

description.en: A Torah Scroll (sefer torah) is a copy of the Hebrew Bible that is written by hand on parchment according to various rules in order to ensure its accuracy, readability, and holiness. The Torah scroll is primarily used in synagogue during Jewish prayer services.
description.he: ספר התורה הוא העתק של חמשת חומשי התורה שנכתב בידי אדם על קלף (נייר העשוי מעור בעלי חיים). כתיבת הספר חייבת להתבצע על פי כללים שנועדו לשמור על הדיוק, על הקדושה ועל קלות הקריאה של הספר. בספר התורה נעשה שימוש בבתי הכנסת בזמן התפילות, כולל בשבת.

description.en: In Ha’azinu (“Listen”) , Moses recites a poem praising God and criticizing the sins of the Israelites. He describes the misfortunes that the Israelites will face and the damage God will ultimately wreak on their oppressors. enBio.value: Moshe ben Nachman, also known as Ramban, was a leading Torah scholar of the middle ages who authored commentaries on Torah and the Talmud. He was a posek who wrote responsa and stand-alone works on Halachic topics, as well as works on mysticism, science and philosophy. Ramban's commentary on the Torah often critiques earlier commentaries and incorporates kabbalistic teachings. He was born in Gerona, Spain, where he established a large yeshiva which produced hundreds of disciples who became leaders of Spanish Jewry. In 1263 he took part in a debate in Barcelona with an apostate Jew named Pablo Christiani, at the behest of the Church. In 1267, at the age of 72, he immigrated to the Holy Land, where he settled in Akko (Acre). He died there at age 76.

description.en: Moshe ben Nachman, also known as Ramban, was a leading Torah scholar of the middle ages who authored commentaries on Torah and the Talmud. He was a posek who wrote responsa and stand-alone works on Halachic topics, as well as works on mysticism, science and philosophy. Ramban's commentary on the Torah often critiques earlier commentaries and incorporates kabbalistic teachings. He was born in Gerona, Spain, where he established a large yeshiva which produced hundreds of disciples who became leaders of Spanish Jewry. In 1263 he took part in a debate in Barcelona with an apostate Jew named Pablo Christiani, at the behest of the Church. In 1267, at the age of 72, he immigrated to the Holy Land, where he settled in Akko (Acre). He died there at age 76.

description.en: Ezekiel was a prophet in the time of the kings Josiah and Jehoiachin who had mystical visions about God's chariot, majesty, and hosts. According to Jewish tradition, accounts of his visions were later written down to make up the book of Ezekiel.

description.en: Edom, meaning “red,” is the name of the country founded by Jacob’s brother Esau, who the Bible says was born “red all over.” Edom was a rival of Israel and later became associated with the Romans and the West. Edom is located in present-day Jordan.

Having a home means that one has a place in which to fulfill such obligations as welcoming guests, placing mezuzot on their door posts, and commemorating the destructions of the Temples. Jewish tradition uses the idea of “home” as a metaphor as well, likening a wife to a home, and imagining God as dwelling in God’s home(s), the [Tabernacle](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) — and then the Temples. Peace in one's home, shalom bayit, is also a priority.

description.en: [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) (“Shir Hashirim”) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. Attributed in its opening verse to [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources), the book records poetic conversations between two lovers, describing their pursuit of each other through vineyards and fields of blossoming flowers. It is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel, and is often read publicly on Passover or on Shabbat evening.

description.en: Pekudei (“Accountings Of”) is the final Torah reading in the Book of Exodus. It describes the making of priestly garments worn in the Mishkan (Tabernacle) and the completion of its construction. At God’s command, Moses erects the Mishkan and puts its vessels in place, and God's presence fills the Mishkan.
description.he: פרשת פקודי, האחרונה בספר שמות, מסכמת את תרומות החומרים השונים למשכן, ואת עשיית בגדי הכהונה. בפרשה מתואר אירוע הקמת המשכן והכנסת הכלים לתוכו. משהושלמה בניית המשכן הענן מכסה את אוהל מועד, והשכינה שורה במשכן. ענן שוכן על המשכן ביום, ובלילה נראית בו אש, לעיני בני ישראל.

titles.text: Eating From the Tree of Knowledge

description.en: Upon placing the first human in the [garden of Eden](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/garden-of-eden?tab=sources), God immediately commands him not to eat from the [tree of knowledge of good and evil](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-tree-of-knowledge?tab=sources), lest he die. A very few verses later, in [Genesis 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.1?lang=bi&with=Rashi&lang2=en), after God has created [Adam's](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam?tab=sources) counterpart, [Eve](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/eve?tab=sources), a [snake](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/snakes1?tab=sources) convinces her to partake of the forbidden fruit, which she in turn shares with Adam. And while Adam, Eve, and the snake are not punished with death, they are punished.

description.en: Chametz refers to leavened [bread](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/bread?tab=sources), understood by the rabbis to be any food containing one of five species of grain — wheat, barley, oat, spelt and rye — that has been allowed to rise. Several biblical verses command that one abstain from consuming chametz on the Passover holiday and to avoid encountering it in other ways.
description.he: חמץ הוא קמח של אחד ממיני הדגן שבא במגע עם מים, וכתוצאה מכך הפך לבצק ותפח. מצווה מרכזית בחג הפסח היא להימנע מאכילת חמץ במשך שבעה ימים, בנוסף למצוות אכילת מצה בליל הסדר. סיבה מרכזית למצוות אלו היא המסורת שבמהלך יציאת מצרים, לחמם של בני ישראל לא הספיק להחמיץ ולתפוח.

description.en: See section 83, where it is explained that spiritual beings are separated and divided from one another by their difference of form. Know that divergent forms, from one extreme to the other, separates these beings and distances them from one extreme to its opposite, until there is no suckling between them at all. As you already know, the supernal light contains only a will to give, not to receive anything, whereas the kelippot have the exact opposite forms: Only a will to receive and to swallow everything; they have no will to give whatsoever. Therefore, they are separated from the Source of Life and are called dead, they and all that cleave to them. This must be understood (Talmud Eser Sefirot, v. 3, Q & A 88).

Masei (“Travels”), the final Torah portion in the Book of Numbers, opens with a list of places that the Israelites traveled in the desert. description.en: Leah is one of the matriarchs of the Jewish people and the first wife of [Jacob](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jacob). Her father tricked Jacob into marrying her and she suffered from the knowledge that she was unloved, in contrast to Jacob's beloved second wife, her sister [Rachel](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/rachel). Kiddush — literally, sanctification — is the ceremonial prayer before the main meals on Shabbat and holidays, recognizing and sanctifying the holy day. It generally includes a blessing on wine and at least one paragraph about the holiness of the day.

description.en: When Sarah struggled with infertility, she gave Abraham her servant, Hagar, to be his concubine. She bore him Ishmael and was afterwards expelled to the desert with her son. They were rescued by an angel and became the ancestors of the Ishmaelites.

description.en: The daughters of Tzelofchad were the only children of the biblical character Tzelofchad. As only men were allowed to inherit their fathers' land, they were concerned that Tzelofchad's land would leave their family. They petitioned Moses and God responded that if a man had no sons, daughters could inherit his land.
description.he: לצלפחד היו חמש בנות, ולא היו לו בנים. הואיל ורק גברים יכלו לרשת את נחלת אבי המשפחה, בנות צלפחד חששו שנחלת אביהן תנושל ממשפחתן. הן ביקשו ממשה שיאפשר להן לרשת את הנחלה, האל נענה להן, ובעקבות בקשתן קבע שאם לאדם אין בנים, בנותיו יכולות לרשת את נחלתו.

description.en: The jubilee (yovel) year is the 50th year in the biblical agricultural cycle and occurs after seven cycles of seven-year shemittah cycles. During the jubilee year, [a shofar is blown on Yom Kippur](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.25.9?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=he&with=all&lang2=he), land ownership resets to its original holders, and all Israelite slaves are set free. Like the [shemittah (sabbatical year)](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shemitah?tab=sources) year, the jubilee year is one in which the land is not worked.

description.en: Viddui is confession of sins. It is said at certain times, such as Yom Kippur and right before one's death. There are different lists of sins that are generally recited — the longest of which, by Rabbeinu Nissim of Bavel, includes hundreds of sins — but it can also be improvised.

enBio.value: Avraham ben Meir ibn Ezra, better known simply as Ibn Ezra, was a medieval Spanish Torah commentator, poet, philosopher and grammarian. While he wrote on grammar, philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and mathematics, he is most famous for his Biblical commentaries, which, alongside those of Rashi, are ubiquitous and indispensable. His commentaries focus on grammatical explanations and the "peshat" (plain-sense) meaning of the text. He often incorporates biting or humorous comments directed toward other commentators, especially towards the Karaites. He maintained a deep friendship with R. Yehudah Halevi, and quotes some of his interpretations in his commentaries. His poetry is still read and sung as part of the regular liturgy. Ibn Ezra knew great poverty and traveled widely, almost incessantly, teaching and making connections with fellow scholars, notably Rabbenu Tam in France.

heBio.value: אברהם בן מאיר אבן עזרא, הידוע כאבן עזרא, היה פרשן תורה ספרדי, משורר, הוגה דעות ומדקדק. אבן עזרא כתב על דקדוק, פילוסופיה, אסטרונומיה, רפואה ומתמטיקה, אך עבודתו המפורסמת ביותר היא פרשנותו לתנ"ך, שבדומה לרש"י, ידועה לכול ויקרת ערך. פרשנות המקרא של אבן עזרא מתמקדת בהסברים דקדוקיים ובמשמעות המילולית (הפשט) של פסוקים. אפשר למצוא בפירושו הערות עוקצניות או הומוריסטיות המכוונות לפרשנים אחרים, ובמיוחד לקראים. השירה שלו עדיין מהווה חלק מן התפילה הקבועה. אבן עזרא חי חיי עוני ונסע כמעט ללא הרף למקומות רבים בעולם, שם הרביץ תורה ברבים ויצר קשרים עם חכמים אחרים, ובעיקר עם רבנו תם מצרפת.

description.en: Avraham ben Meir ibn Ezra, better known simply as Ibn Ezra, was a medieval Spanish Torah commentator, poet, philosopher, and grammarian. A polymath, he wrote on grammar, philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and mathematics. He is most famous for his biblical commentaries, which, alongside those of Rashi, are ubiquitous and indispensable. His commentaries focus on rational, grammatical explanations and the *peshat* (plain sense) meaning of the text. He is often critical of other commentators and especially of Karaites, a group of Jews who rejected the Oral Torah and rabbinic teachings. He maintained a deep friendship with the contemporary Spanish philosopher, [Judah Halevi](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/yehuda-halevi?tab=popular-writing-of), and quotes some of his interpretations in his commentaries. His poetry is still read and sung as part of the regular liturgy. Ibn Ezra knew great poverty and traveled widely, almost incessantly, teaching and making connections with fellow scholars, notably Rabbenu Tam in France.

enBio.value: Nachman of Breslov was one of the most creative chassidic masters, whose thought and teachings continue to resonate within wide circles far beyond his immediate followers. He was a great-grandson of the founder of Chassidut, R. Yisrael Ba'al Shem Tov, and a grandson of another early chassidic master, R. Nachman of Horodenka. Among his many works are a profound presentation of his chassidic and mystical teaching, Likkutei Moharan, and a compilation of his intricate and powerfully evocative stories, Sippurei Ma'asiyot.  Another work relates the events of his transformative journey to and from the Land of Israel. He was severely criticized by certain contemporary chassidic masters, but defended by the leading chassidic master, R. Levi Yitzchak of Berdichev. He moved to Uman less than a year before he passed away from tuberculosis, and his grave there is a pilgrimage site for thousands to this day.

description.en: The world of *Beria* is the second of the four worlds (after the supernal world of *Adam Kadmon*) that emanate and descend from another in the process of creation. According to one explanation, its name is derived from the Hebrew word *bar*, a term that connotes that which is external, implying that the world of *Beria* is a garment for the world of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut). The world of *Beria* parallels the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), or the second [level](/topics/level) of creation, and it is the beginning point of the [enclothing](/topics/enclothe) of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) into a reality that created beings can receive. The world of *Beria* is also called the world of the throne, signifying the Divine lowering itself onto a throne, so to speak, to interact with its creations and the beginning of the revelation of the Divine to lower [levels](/topics/level) of existence. It is also known as the world of souls, since the created entities called souls begin to have significance as receivers of the supernal light. The angelic entities that exist in this world are called *serafim*.

Ahasuerus was the king of Persia in the [book of Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/Esther?tab=contents). He agreed to his advisor Haman's plans to eradicate the Jews and confiscate their property, but his Jewish wife Esther and her cousin Mordekhai foiled the plot when Esther revealed her true identity as a Jew.

description.en: The priestly garments (in Hebrew, bigdei kehunah) were special clothing, primarily made of linen, that were worn by the priests (kohanim) during their service in the [mishkan](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) and later in the Temple. In the book of Exodus, the artisans [Betzalel](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/betzalel?tab=sources) and Oholiav are instructed to make the special garments, which are meant to serve as symbols of "[honor and glory](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.28.2?ven=The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en)."
description.he: בגדי הכהונה הם בגדים מיוחדים שלבשו הכוהנים, משרתי המקדש, בזמן עבודתם בבית המקדש. בגדי הכהונה עשויים בעיקר מפשתן.

description.en: Vayeilech (“He Went”) opens as Moses tells the Israelites that he will not lead them into the Land of Israel, and that Joshua will take over. He instructs the Israelites to gather and read Torah publicly every seven years. At God’s command, Moses writes a poem bearing witness to God’s covenant with the Israelites.
description.he: בפרשת וילך משה מסכם את תקופת הנהגתו ומעביר את ההנהגה ליהושע. מתוארת מצוות הקהל, שהתורה נקראת בה במעמד מיוחד של כל העם שמתקיים בחג הסוכות שבמוצאי שנת השמיטה "במקום אשר יבחר ה'." משה מתאר כיצד בני ישראל ייחטאו בעבודה זרה וייענשו. אלוהים מצווה את משה לכתוב שירה, עדות לבני ישראל.

description.en: The *shalosh regalim* are the three pilgrimage festivals discussed in the Torah: Passover, [Shavuot](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shavuot?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), and [Sukkot](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/sukkot?tab=sources). When the Temple in Jerusalem existed,  people would celebrate these festivals in Jerusalem.
description.he: שלושת הרגלים הם שלושת החגים מן התורה שבה עלו לרגל. בזמן המקדש יהודים היו חוגגים את החגים הללו בירושלים: פסח, שבועות וסוכות.

description.en: Parents feature throughout Jewish contexts in a variety of contexts. The Bible, for example, tells of the patriarchs and matriarchs in the book of Genesis and other parental figures. Rabbinic sources discuss parental responsibilities and obligations of children to their parents.

description.en: The Jewish calendar is a lunarsolar calendar, incorporating elements of a lunar and solar calendar. It consists of 12 months of 29 or 30 days that begin around the time of the new moon, with an extra lunar month added every two or three years. Sources throughout the Jewish textual tradition discuss the development, significance, and legal aspects of the calendar.

description.en: Strength is a trait and value discussed at length in Jewish sources. Biblical stories feature physically strong heroes, such as Samson in the book of Judges. Rabbinic texts  analyze the merits of different types of strength and how they should be valued and prioritized.

description.en: Fruit (p’ri) plays a central role in Judaism, from the forbidden fruit in the Garden of Eden to the seven species — which includes grapes, figs, and pomegranates — brought as first fruit (bikkurim) offerings to the Temple in Jerusalem.

description.he: ארבע אותיות אלה (שבאנגלית נכתבות YHVH) מייצגות את 'השם המפורש' של אלוהים. מסורת יהודית עתיקה אוסרת להגות בקול את השם, ולכן אופן ההגייה המקורי של מילה זו אינו ברור.  במקום זאת, ישנן מגוון של מילים שמחליפות את השם המפורש כמו "אדוניי" ו"השם" בהתאם להקשר.
description.en: The Hebrew letters ‘yud,’ ‘hey,’ ‘vav,’ and ‘hey’ (in English, YHVH) form what is known as the Tetragrammaton, or God’s four-letter name. Given the longstanding Jewish prohibition against speaking God’s name aloud, the word’s original pronunciation is unclear, and it is traditionally not pronounced as written. Instead, a variety of substitutes are used - like “Adonai” (“My Lord”) and “Hashem” (“The Name”) - depending on the context.

description.en: Shemini Atzeret is an early fall holiday that marks the end of the harvest and the start of the rainy season. It directly follows the holiday of [Sukkot](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/sukkot?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) and is observed with prayers for rain in Israel.

description.en: “The Four Children” refers to a rabbinic text incorporated into the *maggid* section of many [haggadahs](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/haggadah?tab=sources). The text presents four types of children who ask different kinds of questions, from different perspectives, at the Passover [seder](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/seder?tab=sources). Each child is given a unique answer, built by weaving together different biblical verses. Variations of the text abound.
description.he: ״ארבעת הבנים״ הוא טקסט מספרות חז״ל שמהווה את אחד החלקים המוכרים יותר בהגדה של פסח. הטקסט מציג ארבעה סוגי ילדים אשר שואלים שאלות המתבססות על פסוקים שונים מספרי שמות ודברים. הטקסט מדריך את ההורים לתת לכל ילד תשובה המתאימה לו ולאישיותו.

description.en: The four species are four plants associated with the holiday of Sukkot. The commandment to gather the four species originates in Leviticus 23:40. Rabbinic sources discuss the exact meaning of each of the phrases in the verse and ultimately identify the four species as: the etrog (citron fruit), lulav (closed frond of a palm tree), hadas (myrtle bough) and aravah (willow branch).
description.he: ארבעת המינים הם ארבעה צמחים הקשורים לחג הסוכות. המקור למצוות ליקוט ארבעת המינים מופיע בפסוק בחומש ויקרא. מקורות רבניים דנים במשמעות המדויקת של כל אחד מהביטויים המופיעים בפסוק זה ובסופו של דבר מזהים את ארבעת המינים כאתרוג, לולב, הדס וערבה.

description.en: Candles (nerot) — or any type of clean-burning oil lamps — are an important feature in the celebration of Shabbat and Jewish holidays. The main function of candles is to provide light in the home at night in order to enhance the festive atmosphere. Candles are also key to Temple and Chanukkah rituals.
description.he: נרות הם מאפיין חשוב בציון שבתות וחגים. הם משמשים להארת הבית בלילה כדי להשרות אווירה חגיגית על הבית. נוסף על כך הנרות ממלאים תפקיד בטקסים של בית המקדש וחג החנוכה.

description.en: Ezra was a priest who, when the Persians conquered the Babylonian empire and allowed the Jews to return, led the Jews to Israel and in rebuilding the Temple. He instituted a series of reforms meant to bring the Jewish people back to their religion.
description.he: עזרא הוא כוהן בתקופת שיבת ציון. אחרי כיבוש בבל על ידי הפרסים, התיר כורש מלך פרס ליהודים לשוב לארץ ישראל ולבנות מחדש את בית המקדש. עזרא עמד בראשם והנהיג סדרה של רפורמות שנועדה להשיב את היהודים למסורת הדתית שלהם.

description.en: Oil features in various contexts in the Jewish textual tradition. In the Bible, oil is used to anoint kings, High Priests, and vessels of the [Tabernacle (mishkan)](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources), as fuel for the [Menorah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/menorah1?tab=sources), and in various biblical stories. Oil also features as an element in food, cosmetics, medicine, and sacrifices, among other functions.
description.he: ברוב המקרים השמן המוזכר בתנ"ך הוא שמן צמחי, ובייחוד כזה המופק מזיתים. השמן מילא תפקיד בפעולות רבות במסורת היהודית, אך השימוש העיקרי בו היה חומר בעֵרה למנורה שבבית המקדש.

description.en: Hannah is a biblical character from the book of Samuel who struggles with infertility. She visits the Tabernacle and prays verbally for a child rather than simply offering a sacrifice. God takes note of her and she gives birth to a son, the prophet Samuel, who would lead the Israelites. In Jewish tradition, Hannah is a model for verbal prayer.
description.he: חנה היא אשת אלקנה ואם שמואל הנביא. היא התמודדה עם עקרות ממושכת, ובמצוקתה הגיעה למשכן בשילה. במקום להקריב קורבן בלבד היא נשאה תפילה בפה לילד, תפילה מילולית. האל שמע את תפילתה, והיא ילדה את שמואל, שבבגרותו היה לנביא ולמנהיג שהוביל את עם ישראל. על פי המסורת, חנה שימשה מודל לתפילה מילולית.

description.en: The Hebrew term *bal tashchit* literally means "Do not destroy" and refers to the biblical prohibition against destroying or wasting that which is yet useful. The initial biblical context of this commandment refers to the needless destruction of fruit-bearing trees. The rabbis of subsequent generations extended this principle to include other kinds of senseless waste.
description.he: בל תשחית (מלשון השחתה) הוא האיסור על הרס סתמי או השלכה ללא צורך של חפצים. אף שבתורה נזכר איסור זה רק ביחס לעצי פרי, חז"ל הבינו שהוא כולל גם סוגים נוספים של השחתה ללא צורך.

description.en: Laban is a biblical character who features in the Book of Genesis. He is the brother of Rebecca, father of Rachel and Leah, and father-in-law of Jacob. His actions are marked by trickery, as he deceptively marries Leah off to Jacob rather than Rachel, and later mistreats Jacob as an employee.

description.he: במקורות נזכר החלב בכמה הקשרים, בהם האיסור לערבב חלב ובשר והתיאור של ארץ ישראל בתור "ארץ זבת חלב ודבש".
description.en: In the Jewish sources, milk (chalav) is discussed generally but also in relation to the laws prohibiting the mixing meat and milk and in the description of Israel as a "land flowing with milk and honey."

description.en: The Copper Altar (Mizbeach Hanechoshet) is the altar upon which sacrifices and libations are offered. The Copper Altar is located within the Temple compound but outside the shrine itself.

description.en: The [book of Ruth](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth.1?lang=bi) is one of the five megillot (scrolls) found in the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings and is traditionally read on the holiday of Shavuot. It tells the story of [Ruth](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/ruth?tab=sources), a widow of Moabite origin, who insists on staying with her widowed, Israelite mother-in-law, declaring “Wherever you go, I will go... your people shall be my people, and your God my God” (1:16). Ruth’s loyalty leads her to the field of her kinsman, Boaz, whom she ultimately marries. Together they have a child, who later becomes the grandfather of King David.
description.he: מגילת רות היא השנייה בקובץ חמש מגילות שבחטיבת הכתובים שבמקרא, ונקראת בחג השבועות. היא מספרת את סיפורה של רות, אלמנה שמוצאה במואב, הדבקה בחמותה האלמנה היהודייה ומצהירה "באשר תלכי אלך, עמך עמי ואלוקייך אלוקיי" (רות א, טז). נאמנותה של רות מוליכה אותה לשדהו של מיטיבה בועז, והוא נושא אותה לאישה. בנם הנולד להם נעשה לימים סבו של דוד המלך.

Naomi is one of the chief figures of the Book of Ruth. She was Ruth's mother-in-law who moved to Moab with her family during a famine, only to return to her home in Bethlehem with Ruth after her husband and sons died. Despondent and poor, she found hope again when Ruth married Boaz and bore a son.

description.en: *Adam Kadmon* is the first and innermost world, which precedes the four worlds of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) ([Emanation](/topics/atzilut)), [*Beria*](/topics/beria1) ([Creation](/topics/beria1)), [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1) ([Formation](/topics/yetzira1)), and [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2) ([Action](/topics/asiya2)). It incorporates all of existence, from its head, that is, the source, which is [*Ein Sof*](/topics/ein-sof1), to its lowest point, which is this physical world. This world is called *Adam Kadmon* because it is depicted in kabbalistic writings in the form of a man, having a head, body and appendages. Although all the worlds are likewise described in the form of a man, this world is the primeval one, before which there is no world, while the other worlds, which are external to it, are “mapped onto it,” lower manifestations of that primeval world: *Atzilut*, from the chest and below to the navel; and *Beria*, *Yetzira*, and *Asiya*, from the navel and below. This world corresponds to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1). Just as [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) itself is often regarded as above the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot), so too the world of *Adam Kadmon* is sometimes not considered part of the four worlds.

The lowest of the four worlds (planes, or [levels](/topics/level) of reality), the world of *Asiya* parallels the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). Accordingly, it is also correlated with the “fourth [level](/topics/level)” of a given structure of reality, like [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), which is the fourth [level](/topics/level) of the five main [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) ([*Keter*](/topics/keter1) is the root [level](/topics/level), followed by the next four, hence, the final [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) is considered “fourth,” as is the plane of *Asiya*). It is called *Asiya*, or “Actualization,” because it is where all the wills and forces that descend from the worlds above it are actualized (*na’asim*), or materialized, within it. The lowest [level](/topics/level) of the world of *Asiya* is our material world that we refer to as “this world.” The spiritual entities that exist in the world of *Asiya* are called *ofanim*, which are the spiritual roots of all that exists in the physical reality of this world.
description.he: העולם התחתון מבין ארבעת העולמות, המשתלשלים זה מזה בתהליך הבריאה. הוא נקרא בשם "עשיה" מפני שבו נעשים ויוצאים בפועל כל הרצונות והכוחות שיש בעולמות שמעליו . הדרגה התחתונה של עולם העשיה היא העולם הגשמי שלנו, <<עולם הזה>>. עולם העשיה מקביל בעניינו לספירת ה<<מלכות>> או ל<<בחינה ד'>>. הישויות של עולם העשיה נקראות "אופנים", מעין מלאכים בדרגה נמוכה, שהם השורשים הרוחניים של כל הנמצא בעולם הזה.

description.en: The destruction of the Temple can refer to the destruction of either of the two Temples that stood in Jerusalem in the ancient period. The First Temple, built by King Solomon, as described in the book of I Kings, was destroyed in 586 BCE by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. The Second Temple, built approximately 70 years after the destruction of the first, was destroyed in 70 CE by the Roman Empire.
description.he: חורבן בית המקדש, או בקיצור ״חורבן הבית״, הוא מושג המתייחס לשני אירועים היסטוריים - חורבן בית המקדש הראשון בשנת 586 לפני הספירה על ידי נבוכדנצר מלך בבל, וחורבן בית המקדש השני בשנת 70 לספירה על ידי טיטוס - קיסר האימפריה הרומית. לעיתים, המושג ״חורבן הבית״ מתייחס באופן נרחב יותר לאיבוד עצמאותו המדינית של עם ישראל בארצו בתקופות אלו. בעקבות החורבן, תיקנו חז״ל 4 ימי תענית: עשרה בטבת - בו התחיל המצור על ירושלים בבית ראשון, י״ז בתמוז - יום ביקוע חומות ירושלים, תשעה באב - הצום העיקרי בו חרבו שני בתי המקדש וצום גדליה - בו נרצח גדליה בן אחיקם אשר היה הנציב היהודי בירושלים לאחר חורבן בית ראשון.

description.en: “Love your neighbor as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18) is the basis for a central principle known as the Golden Rule, or the concept of treating others as one wants to be treated themselves. Much commentary has been penned attempting to understand the verse’s moral message, scope, practical implications, and role in Judaism.
description.he: "ואהבת לרעך כמוך" - מילים שמגיעים מויקרא יט:יח -  הוא אחד העקרונות הידועים והמרכזיים ביהדות אשר מדגיש את חשיבות ההתייחסות לזולת באדיבות, בכבוד ובאמפתיה. הרעיון מאחורי "ואהבת לרעך כמוך" הוא שעלינו לשאוף להתייחס לאחרים כפי שהיינו רוצים שיתייחסו אלינו, באהבה, בחמלה ובהבנה. מושג זה משתקף גם במסורות דתות ומוסריות אחרות, ולעתים קרובות הוא מצוטט כעיקרון מנחה לקידום הרמוניה חברתית, שיתוף פעולה ושיח בין-דתי.

description.en: Usually a reference to a tribal leader.

Tamar was Judah's daughter-in-law. After she married two of his sons who then died, he refused to do his duty by giving her his third son in marriage. Instead, she seduced him by pretending to be a prostitute. She kept his personal effects as a pledge and used them to prove that he owed her his household and protection. The son they had became an ancestor of King David.
description.he: תמר הייתה כלתו של יהודה. היא נישאה לשני בניו, אך שניהם מתו, ולמרות חובתו הוא סירב להשיא לה את בנו השלישי. לפיכך היא התחפשה לזונה ופיתתה את יהודה. היא שמרה את כליו כמשכון והשתמשה בהם להוכחת אחריותו כלפיה. דוד המלך היה מצאצאיו של בנם פרץ.

description.en: Serah is the daughter of [Asher](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/asher?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), son of [Jacob](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jacob?tab=sources). Rabbinic tradition suggests that she never died and has played a few significant roles throughout Jewish history, including telling Jacob the shocking news that Joseph was alive in Egypt and identifying Moses and Aaron as the redeemers of Israel from slavery.
description.he: סרח בת אשר הייתה בתו של אשר בן יעקב. לפי המדרש היא מעולם לא מתה והמשיכה ללוות את בני ישראל בכל מקום שהיו בו.

description.en: Dinah was the daughter of the patriarch [Jacob](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jacob?tab=sources). When she goes out to "visit the daughters of the land," she encounters the prince of Shechem, named Shechem, who takes her by force, rapes her, falls in love with her, and negotiates with her family to marry her. Dismayed upon hearing what has happened and undermining their father's negotiations, Dinah's brothers Simon and Levi take matters into their own hands and slaughter Shechem and all the men of the city and return their sister to her family.
description.he: דינה היא בתו של יעקב אבינו. כאשר יצאה אל העיר שכם, נלקחה בכוח על ידי נסיך העיר, עונתה והוחזקה בארמונו. כנקמה הרגו אחֶיה שמעון ולוי את כל הזכרים בשכם והחזירו את דינה אחותם.

description.en: Lot was Abraham's nephew. As he grew wealthy, his household separated from Abraham's and he settled in Sodom. Angels rescued him and his family when Sodom was destroyed. His daughters thought they were the last living people on earth and had children with him, becoming the ancestors of the Moabites and the Ammonites.

description.en: This is the name for the first and lowest of the five [levels](/topics/level) (and corresponding lights) of the soul, *nefesh*, [*ruaḥ*](/topics/ruah1), [*neshama*](/topics/neshama2), [*ḥaya*](/topics/haya1), and [*yeḥida*](/topics/yehida1). These five [levels](/topics/level) of the soul correspond to the five primary *sefirot*, of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), as well as the five worlds, [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2), [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut), [*Beria*](/topics/beria1), [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1), and [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2). The concept of the five [levels](/topics/level) of the soul relates to five qualities of supernal light which illuminate people as well as the [levels](/topics/level) of broader reality. The *nefesh* corresponds to and is the light that belongs to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) and the world of [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2), and it is the first aspect of the soul that is illuminated within a person or an aspect of reality.

description.en: *Adam Kadmon* is the first and innermost world, which precedes the four worlds of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) ([Emanation](/topics/atzilut)), [*Beria*](/topics/beria1) ([Creation](/topics/beria1)), [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1) ([Formation](/topics/yetzira1)), and [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2) ([Action](/topics/asiya2)). It incorporates all of existence, from its head, that is, the source, which is [*Ein Sof*](/topics/ein-sof1), to its lowest point, which is this physical world. This world is called *Adam Kadmon* because it is depicted in kabbalistic writings in the form of a man, having a head, body and appendages. Although all the worlds are likewise described in the form of a man, this world is the primeval one, before which there is no world, while the other worlds, which are external to it, are “mapped onto it,” lower manifestations of that primeval world: *Atzilut*, from the chest and below to the navel; and *Beria*, *Yetzira*, and *Asiya*, from the navel and below. This world corresponds to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1). Just as [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) itself is often regarded as above the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot), so too the world of *Adam Kadmon* is sometimes not considered part of the four worlds.

enBio.value: Yosef Karo, expelled from Spain as a child, was a rabbi, Talmudist, mystic and the pre-emiment halachic codifier. His best-known work, the Shulchan Aruch, was accepted in his lifetime and formally recognized thereafter as the definitive statement of Jewish legal and religious practice. He also wrote basic commentaries on the Mishneh Torah and the Arba'ah Turim (the latter forming the basis from which the Shulchan Aruch was distilled). He was also a mystic who received heavenly revelations. Some of these were set down in writing and formed the impetus to come to the Land of Israel. There, he lived in Tsfat, where he took a central role in the attempt by his teacher, Rabbi Yaakov Berav, to revive traditional rabbinic Semikhah.

description.en: Joseph Karo, expelled from Spain as a child, was a rabbi, talmudist, mystic, and preemiment halakhic codifier. His best-known work, the Shulchan Arukh, was accepted in his lifetime and formally recognized thereafter as the definitive statement of Jewish legal and religious practice. He also wrote basic commentaries on Rambam's Mishneh Torah and Jacob ben Ashe's Arba'ah Turim, both of which were major sources for his own Shulchan Arukh. As a mystic, he also received heavenly revelations. Some of these were set down in writing and contributed to his decision to migrate to the land of Israel. There, he lived in Safed, where he supported the effort of his teacher, Rabbi Yaakov Berav, to revive traditional rabbinic ordination (Hebrew: semikhah).

description.en: The second constriction occurred in one of the formative stages of the [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf) of [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2) , in order to enable the creation of man and this world. The fourth [level](/topics/level), or phase of creation, which constitutes the will to receive, or the attribute of judgment, also known as the [level](/topics/level) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), rose and mingled with the second [level](/topics/level), which constitutes the will to give, or the attribute of mercy, also known as the [level](/topics/level) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), and thus the [partition](/topics/partition2) that is upon the [level](/topics/level) [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) rose to the second [level](/topics/level) as well. As a consequence of the [partition](/topics/partition2)’s new position, the light of the [levels](/topics/level) beneath the second [level](/topics/level), the third and fourth [levels](/topics/level), was darkened. It is this intermingling of the will to give with the will to receive that creates the capacity for free choice between these options for human beings.

description.en: Meribah is a place mentioned in the books of Exodus and Numbers. In one story in Exodus, the Israelites complain about a lack of water. God instructs Moses to hit a rock; Moses does, and water comes out. The place is then called Massah and Meribah, commemorating the incident. In a similar story described in Numbers, God instructs Moses to take his staff and talk to a rock after the Israelites complain about a lack of water. Moses hits the rock twice and water comes out. God then tells Moses and Aaron that they will not enter Israel, and refers to the water as "water of Meribah."

Rabi (Rabbi Yehuda haNasi) succeeded his father, R. Shimon ben Gamliel as Nasi and was a key figure in Jewish history. A pious and brilliant scholar, he worked to further consolidate the authority of his office. His great wealth and his prestige among the Jews also impressed the Romans, resulting in many discussions with them. His greatest achievement, however, was his organization and compilation of Jewish Law in the Mishnah.

description.en: Hatarat Nedarim (the annulment of vows) is a legal process which allows one to cancel a vow by reciting a text in the presence of three people. It is customary to perform hatarat nedarim in the days leading up to [Rosh HaShanah](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah?tab=contents) or [Yom Kippur](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/yom-kippur?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), in a version of the ceremony that involves cancelling all vows taken in the past and to be taken in the future.

Renewal is a concept that can involve revitalizing, reinvigorating, or returning to an original state. In Judaism, the term can be used to refer to a specific 20th-century Jewish movement, but  is also a concept found throughout biblical and rabbinic literature. The idea is particularly prevalent throughout chasidic texts, which emphasize performing routine commandments as if it were one’s first time performing them.
description.he: התחדשות היא רעיון חזרת המצב לקדמותו לאחר שינוי, או היווספות פרטים ומאפיינים חדשים לדבר קיים. ביהדות, המושג יכול להתייחס לתנועה יהודית ספציפית במאה ה-20 אשר שמה דגש על הרעננות והחיוניות בחוויה האלוהית, או למושג שמופיע רבות בתנ״ך ובספרות חז״ל. ניתן למצוא את רעיון ההתחדשות גם בספרי חסידות רבים המדגישים את חשיבות יישום רעיון זה בקיום המצוות המעשיות.

description.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was esteemed as the second most prominent student of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, establishing his own academy in Peki'in and emerging as a rival to Rabbi Eliezer. Despite his independent stance, Rabbi Yehoshua's disagreements with Rabban Gamliel led to eventual submission. This transformation elevated him to become the most influential scholar of his era.
description.he: רבי יהושע נחשב שני לרבי אליעזר בין תלמידי רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. הוא ייסד בית מדרש בפקיעין והפך לבר־פלוגתא של רבי אליעזר. חשיבתו העצמאית הביאה אותו לידי עימות גם עם רבן גמליאל, אך בסופו של דבר הוא נכנע לסמכותו והיה לחכם המשפיע ביותר של תקופתו.

description.en: Moving from Babylonia to Israel around the same time as his uncle, Rav Chiyya, Rav studied in Rabbi' Yehudah haNasi's academy. Not finding his place there, he moved back to eventually set up an academy in Sura. His academy came to rival Shmuel's academy in Nehardea, as the fame of Rav's wisdom and learning spread far and wide. Besides his many legal decisions and interpretations, he wrote many prayers that are still in use.
description.he: רב עלה לארץ ישראל באותה תקופה שעלה דודו, רבי חייא, ולמד בבית מדרשו של רבי יהודה הנשיא. מאחר שלא מצא שם את מקומו, חזר לבבל וייסד את הישיבה בסורא. ברבות השנים, עם פרסום חוכמתו ותלמודו של רב, הייתה ישיבה זו יריבה של ישיבת נהרדעא בראשות שמואל. נוסף על פועלו בתחום ההלכה והפרשנות חיבר תפילות רבות הנאמרות עד עצם היום הזה.

description.en: Rabbi Eliezer b. Hyrcanus was a rabbinic sage in the first and second centuries CE and one of the most frequently quoted rabbis in the Mishnah. Considered to be [R. Yochanan b. Zakkai's](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/rabban-yochanan-b-zakkai?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) greatest student, R. Eliezer was nevertheless a controversial figure. Coming from a wealthy but uneducated family, he left them to study Torah in poverty and eventually directed an academy in Lod. Highly conservative in his approach to Torah, he was isolated and eventually excommunicated by his colleagues.
description.he: רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס נחשב לתלמידו המזהיר של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ואף על פי כן היה דמות שנויה במחלוקת. הוא עזב את משפחתו העשירה אך חסרת הרקע בלימוד תורה כדי ללמוד תורה במצב של עוני, והתקדם עד שעמד בראש ישיבה בלוד. מאחר שיחסו לתורה היה שמרני ביותר, בחלוף השנים נידו אותו עמיתיו .

description.en: Shacharit is the morning service. It consists of four main sections: Preparatory prayers and readings; Shema and its blessings, the Shemoneh Esrei; and the concluding sections. The Torah is read on Mondays and Thursdays, as well as on Shabbat and most special days.
description.he: שחרית היא תפילת הבוקר. בתפילה זו כלולים ארבעה חלקים עיקריים: קטעי הכנה וקריאה מקדימים, קריאת שמע וברכותיה, תפילת עמידה (שמונה־עשרה) וקטעי סיום. התורה נקראת בימים שני וחמישי, בשבת ובמועדים.

description.en: Often translated as bounty, flow, or abundance, *shefa* comes from the Hebrew word *hashpa’a*, which in this context means to give. Rays of sunlight, for example, can be described as the sun’s *shefa*. The rays constitute a “flow” of light from the sun that provides light and sustenance to the earth in bountiful abundance. In kabbalistic thought, *shefa*  refers to different forms of light that flow from God's essence or from the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) and the like. Additionally, *shefa* can be used to refer both to God’s giving to creation, as well as the giving of created beings to each other.

description.en: The bringing forth of something into existence ex nihilo, [*yesh* *me*’*ayin*](/topics/yesh-meayin), is known as *Beria* (Creation). Since the [opacity](/topics/opacity) ([*ovyut*](/topics/ovyut)) in the vessels cannot be revealed in the world of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) ([Emanation](/topics/atzilut)), but only from the ground of the world of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) ([Emanation](/topics/atzilut)) and below, it is therefore called *Beria* from that point and below, after the [opacity](/topics/opacity) ([*ovyut*](/topics/ovyut)) that has been revealed. For the [opacity](/topics/opacity) ([*ovyut*](/topics/ovyut)), which is comprised of the [will to receive](/topics/will-to-receive) in the created being, is a form of [*yesh* *me*’*ayin*](/topics/yesh-meayin), creation from nothing. Everything that exists is drawn from God as *yesh miyesh*, literally “something from something,” because there is nothing He does not have, apart from a “will of receiving,” which of necessity He does not possess, since there is no one from whom He could receive, God forbid. This must be understood.

Rest is the abstention from creative work. After the six days of creation, God rested, and the fourth of the Ten Commandments — Shabbat — is to cease from creative work and rest just as God did. The Torah also commands that the land of Israel be left to lie fallow every seventh year in observance of [shemittah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shemitah?tab=sources). Rest is also required on holidays. While rest is the means of renewing our bodies and souls, tradition also recognizes it as a taste of the world to come.

Kaddish is an Aramaic prayer that declares praise of God. Its four main variants punctuate Jewish prayer services, marking the end of each section and its conclusion. It describes God's holiness and greatness and calls for the recognition of God's eternal rule over all of mankind. It is only recited in the presence of a prayer quorum and is further adapted for different contexts, including burials and to mark ritually the conclusion of a significant body of learning, a siyyum.

description.en: The world of *nekudim* is the second of the worlds of [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2). It is called by this name because the spiritual [levels](/topics/level) within it are called *nekudot*, or points. In this context, the *nekuda* refers to [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), the fourth [level](/topics/level), after the first [constriction](/topics/constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)) occurred. As a result of this constriction, [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) is only a black point without any light whatsoever.Then,as a result of the [second constriction](/topics/second-constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)), [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) and the [partition](/topics/partition2) that is upon it became intermingled within all the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) and are then present in all the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). As a result of this intermingling, there are ten *nekudot*, or ten *Malkhuyot* with [partitions](/topics/partition2) because the [level](/topics/level) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) with its [partition](/topics/partition2) is present in each of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). This contrasts with the preceding worlds, in which there was only one [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) and one [partition](/topics/partition2). The world of *nekudim* is also called the “world of breaking,” or the “world of chaos,” because the shattering of the vessels occurred in this world.

description.en: The destruction of the Temple can refer to the destruction of either of the two Temples that stood in Jerusalem in the ancient period. The First Temple, built by King Solomon, was destroyed in 586 BCE by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. The Second Temple, built 70 years after the destruction of the first, was destroyed in 70 CE by the Roman empire. The fast day of Tisha B'Av commemorates the destruction of both Temples, among other historical tragedies.

The Menorah is a large candelabra with seven branches that is located within the Temple shrine. The Menorah is lit and cleaned by the priests every day. The Menorah used on Hanukkah is called a Hanukkiah, and it has nine branches.

description.en: Although the supernal light wishes to permeate every [level](/topics/level) of reality, reality cannot fully contain it on account of its limited vessels, or receptacles. Therefore the supernal light that cannot be contained, called surrounding light, is always situated in the background and so has an indirect influence on reality. This contrasts with the [inner light](/topics/inner-light1), which is the supernal light that is currently [enclothed](/topics/enclothe) in reality and permeates it in accordance with the reality’s capacity to contain it. When reality is fully rectified in the future, the surrounding light too will be able to permeate it.

*Kelippot* are [levels](/topics/level) of reality that do not contain any will to give, only the will to receive. Since their essence is one of receiving or “taking,” they are constantly trying to pull all of reality into themselves – in essence, to swallow everything in existence. Since the essence of life is the divine light, which is composed entirely of the energy of giving, they and all that is connected to them are considered to be “dead.” The *kelippot* are therefore compared to the husks or shells of a fruit, which are detached from the life that is inside the fruit. Since these entities are wholly receiving, unable to give, they have no true connection with the life force of creation, like the dead.

Elisha b. Abuya was the son of a rich merchant and a student of [R. Akiva](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/rabbi-akiva?tab=sources). He too became disoriented when he "entered the orchard." In his case, he turned against the Torah and opposed it. His abandonment of the Torah results in his coming to be known as "Acher," or "the other one."  [R. Meir](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/rabbi-meir?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) was his disciple and treated him with the utmost respect, even after he left the fold. Not only did R. Meir encourage him to repent while alive, he seemingly saved Elisha's soul once he died.
description.he: אלישע בן אבויה היה בנו של סוחר עשיר ותלמידו של רבי עקיבא. גם הוא כחבריו התבלבל כאשר "נכנס לפרדס", אבל שלא כמוהם, הוא כפר בתורה. רבי מאיר המשיך להיות תלמידו גם אחרי שכפר, ולא רק שדחק בו לחזור בתשובה בחייו, אלא מסופר שהציל את נשמתו של אלישע ברגע מותו.

The story describes how people attempted to build a city and tower, the top of which would reach the sky. God confounds their speech and scatters them, ending the project. The story has been the subject of much analysis and discussion throughout thousands of years of the Jewish textual tradition.

When Jacob blessed his sons, he gave Reuven a mixed one, due to Reuven having had an affair with Bilhah, Jacob's concubine.

description.en: Adar is the sixth month of the Hebrew calendar. In seven out of every 19 years, a second month of Adar is added in order to keep the agricultural cycle of the Jewish lunar calendar synchronized with the solar year. [The rabbis taught](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.29a.18?vhe=William_Davidson_Edition_-_Vocalized_Aramaic&lang=bi) that one rejoices when the month of Adar begins.

description.en: The twelve spies feature in the books of Numbers and Deuteronomy. They were a group of leaders - one from each tribe - sent by Moses to scout the land of Canaan ahead of the Israelites arrival there. They came back reporting that the land was good, but that it was filled with giants and fearsome enemies. This prompted the Israelites to cry and complain that they did not want to enter the land. Two of the twelve spies, Joshua and Caleb, attempted to assuage their fears and remind the people of God’s commitment that the Israelites’ would enter the land.

description.en: After the destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple in 70 CE, Rabban Yochanan b. Zakkai moved the Sanhedrin to Yavneh, which became an important center of Jewish learning, rabbinic scholarship, and the development of modern Judaism as it is known today.
description.he: לאחר חורבן ירושלים ובית המקדש השני בשנת 70 לספירה העביר רבן יוחנן בן זכאי את הסנהדרין ליבנה. עם השנים הייתה יבנה למרכז חשוב של לימוד תורה והלכה וכן של פיתוח היהדות המוכרת לנו היום.

description.en: Niggun is a melody, generally unaccompanied by words. In the Bible, it is often associated with uplifting or calming properties. Its spiritual potential was reclaimed in Chasidut, such that one of the common duties of a Chasidic rebbe is to sing, and sometimes even compose, melodies.
description.he: ניגון הוא מלודיה שבדרך כלל איננה מלווה במילים. על פי רוב בתנ"ך לניגון תכונות מרוממות או משרות רוגע. החסידות הדגישה את הפוטנציאל הרוחני של הניגון: אחד התפקידים של האדמו"ר החסידי הוא שירה, ולפעמים גם חיבור ניגונים.

description.en: The priestly service consisted of ritual worship carried out by priests in the [Tabernacle (Mishkan)](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) and later in the Temple. The service included offering daily sacrifices, cleaning and preparing the altar for sacrifice, arranging the [menorah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/menorah1?tab=sources) for lighting, offering the [ketoret](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/incense?tab=sources), and more. Particulars of the service are discussed in detail in the [book of Leviticus](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus?tab=contents) and in the fifth order of the Mishnah and Talmud, [Kodashim](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Mishnah/Seder%20Kodashim).

description.en: Eve was the first woman, the "mother of all," created by being separated from [Adam's](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam?tab=sources) body. In the [garden of Eden](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/garden-of-eden?tab=sources), the snake convinced Eve to try the forbidden fruit of the [tree of knowledge](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-tree-of-knowledge?tab=sources), from which she also gave to Adam. The result was that they were both expelled from the garden and that she and all of womankind would be cursed to endure difficult [childbirths](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/birth?tab=sources) even as they desire their husbands, to whom they are subject.
description.he: חוה היא האישה הראשונה מבנות מינה ואם כל חי. היא נוצרה מצלעו של אדם והופרדה ממנו. הנחש בגן עדן שכנע אותה לטעום מפרי עץ הדעת, וממנו האכילה גם את אדם. בעקבות זאת גורשו שניהם מגן עדן, ובנות מינה קוללו בלידות קשות ובשיעבוד לגברים.

Havdalah — literally, separation — is the ritual that marks the end of Shabbat, separating it from the rest of the week. It consists of blessings over wine, fire, and sweet fragrances, and the separation between holy time and non-holy time, light and darkness, and Israel and the nations.
description.he: הבדלה היא טקס המציין את צאת השבת. ההבדלה כוללת אמירת ברכה על יין, נר ובשמים ועוסקת במושג ההבחנה, או ההבדלה, על ידי השוואת ההבדלה בין השבת וימות השבוע להבדלה בין אור וחושך.

description.en: The tree of knowledge is a tree that features in the opening chapters of the [book of Genesis](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis?tab=contents). God causes the tree to grow in the [Garden of Eden](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/garden-of-eden?tab=sources), and commands [Adam](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam?tab=sources) not to eat from it, lest he die. In the following chapter, [Eve](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/eve?tab=sources), following the enticing of a snake, notices the desirable qualities of a tree in the Garden. She eats from the tree's fruits and gives to Adam as well. God then calls out to Adam, and describes consequences that the snake, Eve, and Adam will each face as a result of their actions.

description.en: The Cave of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs — or ma'arat hamakhpelah in Hebrew — is the area in Hebron that Abraham purchased as a burial place for his wife Sarah in [Genesis 23](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.23.1?lang=bi&with=Navigation&lang2=en). As the family tomb of the patriarchs and many of matriarchs of the Jewish people, it is considered a holy site and is a pilgrimage destination and site of prayer.

description.en: This is the name for the second of the five [levels](/topics/level) (and corresponding light) of the soul: [*nefesh*](/topics/nefesh), [*ruaḥ*](/topics/ruah1), [*neshama*](/topics/neshama2), [*ḥaya*](/topics/haya1), and [*yeḥida*](/topics/yehida1). These five [levels](/topics/level) of the soul correspond to the five primary *sefirot*, [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), as well as the five worlds, [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2), [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut), [*Beria*](/topics/beria1), [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1), and [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2). The *ruaḥ* [level](/topics/level) of the soul corresponds to and is the light of the [level](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) and the world of [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1). A person attains the illumination of this aspect of the soul after first attaining the illumination of the lowest part, which is the [*nefesh*](/topics/nefesh).

description.en: The Red Sea (Yam Suf in Hebrew) — often mistranslated as the Reed Sea — is located along Egypt's eastern border. The Egyptians though pursued the Israelites into the Red Sea, wherein they drowned.
